TinySHell_0.7_gcc13_x64_tsh.notes: Christophe Devine's minimal encrypted backdoor, built as the two binaries one tree produces: tshd (the implanted server, the component that matters) and tsh (the client). Mandiant's March 2025 UNC3886 reporting links this repository for six TINYSHELL-derived Junos backdoors (appid, to, irad, lmpad, jdosd, oemd) and keys its hunting rule on tsh_get_file, tsh_put_file, tsh_runshell, tshd_get_file, tshd_put_file and tshd_runshell, all present here. Those samples are FreeBSD/Junos, so these Linux ELF artefacts are a toolchain proxy for them rather than a container match. Symbol-carrying functions: tsh 44 / tshd 34 on x86, tsh 33 / tshd 29 on x64, of which 20 in tshd are the project's own on both. Linked dynamically, so glibc is not in the image under this family's name - the trap -static set for monomorph. aes.c and sha1.c are Devine's own implementations and the direct ancestors of XySSL, PolarSSL and mbedTLS, which is four versions and 26 artefacts here: not duplicates twenty years apart, but the same author's same algorithms, so read the cross-family PicHash census for this family with that in mind, as with libsodium's ed25519-ref10. The aes.c and sha1.c self-test main() functions sit inside #ifdef TEST (aes.c:585, sha1.c:259) and are compiled out, so linking all four translation units raises no duplicate main - correcting the concern recorded in issue #52. Upstream disagrees with itself on the version: Makefile:13 says tsh-0.7, tsh.c:2 says 0.6.
